facts.statement: The species Fenghuangopterus lii was described and named in 2010 by Lü Junchang and colleagues.
facts.quote: The type species Fenghuangopterus lii was in 2010 described and named by Lü Junchang et al.

facts.statement: The specific name honors Li Xiumei, the fossil's donor.
facts.quote: The specific name honors Li Xiumei, who donated the fossil.

facts.statement: The animal is known from a single, crushed holotype skeleton found in the Tiaojishan Formation of Liaoning Province, dating to about 160 million years ago.
facts.quote: It is known from a single relatively complete, though badly crushed, fossil skeleton, holotype CYGB-0037, recovered from the Tiaojishan Formation of Liaoning Province, about 160 million years old.

facts.statement: It possessed eleven teeth in the upper jaw that extended further back than in its relatives.
facts.quote: The primary differences between Fenghuangopterus and other scaphognathines reside in its more numerous teeth — eleven in the upper jaw — which extended further back in the jaw than with its relatives

facts.statement: Fenghuangopterus belongs to the subfamily Scaphognathinae, which was previously known only from the Late Jurassic.
facts.quote: Fenghuangopterus is a member of the rhamphorhynchid subfamily Scaphognathinae, which had previously been known only from the Late Jurassic

facts.statement: It is a Rhamphorhynchid of the subfamily Scaphognathinae, which includes the genera Scaphognathus, Sordes, and Harpactognathus.
facts.quote: Es un Rhamphorhynchidae de la subfamilia Scaphognathinae, de la que hasta ahora solo se conocían fósiles del Jurásico Superior, e incluye los géneros Scaphognathus, Sordes y Harpactognathus.

facts.statement: The animal lived between 168.2 and 152.21 million years ago, spanning the Bathonian to Kimmeridgian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Bathonian to Kimmeridgian (168.2 to 152.21 million years ago)
